_purpose: Stage-4 alert state machine thresholds. SEPARATE from the locked M8_threshold_config.json. Derived by measuring the PRODUCTION TCN-AE live score_C on disk with a fill-matched protocol. ISA-18.2 record.
_floor_location_note: Active floors live in state_machine.rolling_mean_100_floor / rolling_mean_200_floor (where step23/step1c wrote them and where load_alert_thresholds reads them). These TOP-LEVEL keys are an identical mirror per Step-5 handoff P2 in case a future loader reads top-level. Keep both in sync.

_provenance_step5.comment: Floors > p99 of sigma=0.045 simulator baseline. Steady-state noise cannot trip WARN; in-envelope compound faults still escalate.

score_C.polarity_note: AUC is direction-agnostic. Alarm logic assumes fault score_C > normal. Ordering is decided on MEDIAN separation (normal < groupB <= confirmed), the same robust statistic as the polarity check, so ordering and polarity are consistent by construction and reproducible (v2 used tail percentiles that flipped run-to-run under CUDA float nondeterminism). Tail percentiles below are provenance only and do NOT drive the tier.

reliability_policy.STRONG: score_C may drive up to DANGER
reliability_policy.WEAK: score_C may contribute to WARN only; never sole DANGER
reliability_policy.UNUSABLE: score_C advisory-only; drives no state transition

serve_reality.note: At live stride=50, normal (200-step) sequences cannot fill MIN_READY windows, so score_C does NOT establish a normal baseline on the 1 Hz route. score_C is a slow chain signal (full 63-window buffer ~= 52 min at 1 Hz). Step 4.3 must NOT expect score_C to fire on short/acute windows; score_A (MAE) is the acute path.

state_machine._step6_slope_update: Step 6 (29-May-2026): slope_warn raised 0.0003 -> 0.002. ROOT CAUSE of G1_normal_fpr=100%: mech_B_slope fired every window because the live sigma=0.045 baseline yields an OLS score_A slope ~0.00032 >= 0.0003. The path is also non-separating for its intended target: Label-21 gradual wear slope ~0.00015 < baseline noise 0.00032, so slow-drift detection belongs to CUSUM (L3, G4a PASS), NOT the direct-slope WARN.
